system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.

To make the results easier to read, the students started to put the information into the bar graph.

Complete the bar graph.

[Image: Bar graph]

Figure, described in words:
An incomplete bar graph titled "Car Speed". The vertical axis is labeled "Number of Cars" with tick marks and numerical labels at 0, 5, and 10. The horizontal axis has tick marks dividing it into three category columns labeled "Slow", "Medium", and "Fast". A single light-gray shaded rectangular bar is drawn in the "Slow" column, reaching a height of approximately 9 (just below the tick mark for 10). The "Medium" and "Fast" columns are currently empty.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer: Counting the table: Slow = cars 2,3,6,9,10,11,13,16,18 = 9 cars (matches the existing bar). Medium = cars 1,7,8,12,17,19 = 6 cars. Fast = cars 4,5,14,15,20 = 5 cars. To complete the graph, I would draw a bar in the Medium column reaching exactly 6 (one tick mark above the 5 line, just above the midpoint between 5 and 10), and a bar in the Fast column reaching exactly 5 (level with the tick mark labeled 5). Check: 9 + 6 + 5 = 20 cars.
